note: PHASE 10.1 -- SLOT 2 (make the receipt failure LOUD). Ricky chose the smallest fix that would have caught all three of today failures, over refusing cross-tree mints or the broader text-only-review work. ROOT CAUSE, proven not theorised: REPO_ROOT in review-scope.mjs is path.resolve(__dirname,"..","..") -- derived from the MODULE own file location -- so a review stamps the tree whose copy of the module it loaded, regardless of which diff it read. Demonstrated live: the same import resolves STAMP_PATH to C:/tmp/wc-c0 from the worktree and C:/dev/Website from the main checkout. With git worktrees that is two independent receipts. On 2026-08-04 three consecutive /code-review runs failed to receipt the Slot 1 ship: the first produced empty output, the second targeted the wrong tree, and the THIRD reported CLEAN while describing a different branch diff (stripSource.mjs, check-image-widths.mjs, as-never cast removals -- #184 and #139 files, none of them in the ship). The gate refused correctly every time; the receipt mechanism was never the weak link. What was missing was any way to TELL, so an operator re-runs the review in the same wrong place and gets the same red. FIX: stamps now carry a provenance block (repo_root, branch, head), and ship-gate names the mismatch instead of saying only "no valid review stamp found". DELIBERATELY NOT A GATE CHANGE -- coverage is still decided by content hash alone; provenance explains a miss and must never create one, which is its own spec. The silent directions are asserted as hard as the loud one: a pre-provenance stamp, a matching stamp, and a git that cannot answer all produce NO note, or the gate cries wolf on every honest ship. REVIEW FOLD (8 findings, all folded as edits): the HIGH one corrected a DESIGN error, not an implementation slip -- the repo_root comparison could not fire for the failure it was written for. The stamp lives at REPO_ROOT/.claude/, so any stamp the gate can READ was by construction written by a module rooted in that same directory; it compared a directory against itself. The 2026-08-04 miss does not present as a mismatched root, it presents as NO STAMP AT ALL. The actual cure is printing STAMP_PATH on the ABSENT branch, which costs nothing and works precisely when the stamp is missing. Provenance survives as the BRANCH check plus belt-and-braces for a stamp arriving by copy or junction, with the limit recorded in the docblock so nobody mistakes the field for the cure. Also folded: case-folded root compare on win32, kept as belt-and-braces only (an EARLIER version of this record claimed c:/ vs C:/ was the NORM because the mint resolves a relative argv path and the gate an absolute one -- that was WRONG and a later review caught it: both sides default to the same module-derived REPO_ROOT constant, and nothing in scripts/ calls git rev-parse --show-toplevel except session-lock.mjs, so in the ordinary case the compare is a string against itself; the folding earns its keep only for an injected root or a stamp arriving by copy, junction or symlink); a dead || expression that could only ever return its fallback at the cost of two git subprocesses; root now doubles as the git cwd so a record cannot claim tree A path beside tree B branch; the branch note no longer says "does not speak for this ship" (content hashing means it DOES cover what it stamped) and no longer prints branch HEAD during a rebase; the note is emitted ONCE at the end rather than per file, which also reaches "changed after review" and both deletion reasons; and mergeReviewStamp is PURE again -- the describeProvenance() default had ~30 unit call sites shelling out to git and meant the path production relied on was the one path no spec exercised. R4 canary: tests/reviewStampProvenance.test.ts, 11 specs, 3-mutation battery all caught. Two defects found by the specs during authoring and fixed: describeProvenance did not swallow a THROWING injected run (only the gitSoft default caught), and a green verdict carries an informational reason line. Authoring pin: claude-opus-5 / high; session runs claude-opus-5[1m] / high -- effort matches, [1m] variant declared. Worktree C:/tmp/wc-prov, branch ci/review-stamp-provenance, cut from origin/main 405712e. SLOT 1 IS PARKED, NOT ABANDONED: C:/tmp/wc-c0 on ci/integrity-control-bytes, 9 files staged, pre-ship PASSED, awaiting a receipt minted by a mechanism that can now be trusted to report where it ran. SECOND FOLD (the FIFTH receipt failure, and the close of the text-only gap). A sixth /code-review ran in this tree and again minted NOTHING -- this time it said WHY: ReportFindings was not in the agent toolset (select:ReportFindings plus two keyword searches returned nothing), so the findings arrived as prose. Per Ricky standing decision, retrying stopped there and the mint path was fixed instead. Its 4 findings were reproduced independently and folded as edits: (1) MEDIUM, the provenance note pushed into warnings corrupted the green coverage count, since covered = totalScope - warnings.length assumes every warning is a file -- reproduced live at -1 of 1 risky file(s) covered; notes now travel in their own channel and the count is taken before any diagnostic could join it; (2) that note printed under the unreviewed app code (advisory) banner, announcing a diagnostic as an unreviewed source file -- now a neutral label; (3) the branch note claimed files it already stamped stay covered by content hash even for a STALE stamp, which covers nothing -- the note is now offered only for a fresh stamp; (4) the sameRoot docblock (and this record) described a mechanism the codebase does not use -- corrected above. THE MINT-PATH FIX: /code-review is a built-in skill, so its toolset cannot be granted ReportFindings from this repo -- the gap is structural on our side and the cure is detection, not prevention. The hook now journals EVERY invocation to .claude/.review-mint-log.json (gitignored, per-tree, like the stamp), counting genuine ReportFindings payloads separately from bare script runs, and ship-gate consults it whenever no stamp is present. The sentence that would have saved five runs today now prints: the ReportFindings mint has NEVER fired in this tree -- a /code-review whose agent lacks that tool reports its findings as TEXT, mints nothing, and looks identical here to no review at all. KNOW THE LIMIT: a text-only review leaves no trace of its own; this answers the prior question (has the mechanism ever worked here?), it does not observe the review. Deliberately NOT a gate change -- it gates nothing and is silent when the journal cannot be read or written. Guarded against the inverse cry-wolf: a hand-run script (empty stdin, refused) records genuine:false and never vouches for the wiring. record defaults to a NO-OP inside runHook with the real writer supplied by the isMain block, so the ten existing runHook specs cannot each append a genuine fire to this tree journal and have the gate vouch for the mint on the strength of a test run. Verification: 35 specs in reviewStampProvenance (11 new), 188/188 across the three receipt suites, two mutation batteries (3 + 4) all caught with every touched file restored byte-identical, and both journal states proven end-to-end against the real CLI. .claude/settings.local.json drifted into the diff AGAIN (mojibake re-encodes plus a permission delta, the PR #163 class) and was RESTORED, not shipped -- expect it every session. STILL OPEN: slot 3 (check-sourcemap-debugids.mjs:79-82), and this ship still needs a receipt minted by a mechanism it cannot mint for itself.
